content:
Blog author Nicolas Lellouche, while test-driving the iPhone Duo, examined its settings options carefully. He discovered a rather interesting new option in the display settings called "Shift Left Edge".

When this setting is enabled, a black border is added to the left side of the screen, effectively adding an artificial bezel beyond the outer screen's edge, pushing the displayed content away from the fold.

The description within the iPhone Duo's system for this setting states that it "adjusts the content display position when using a case that partially covers the left edge of the outer screen".

As seen in his short video demonstration, after enabling this setting, the black border on the left edge of the iPhone Duo's outer screen roughly doubled in width.

It remains unclear which types of cases would require this setting to be enabled.

Apple will offer two original case accessories for the iPhone Duo at launch: the iPhone Duo Case and the iPhone Duo Folio with stand functionality.

Without hands-on testing, it's difficult to determine whether these cases will noticeably cover the left edge and affect screen content display, but it doesn't appear to be an issue. Apple may be anticipating this setting will apply to other styles offered by third-party accessory makers—possibly more rugged and durable case designs.

Further details will have to wait until closer to launch to confirm. The iPhone Duo will officially go on sale next month on October 23.
